articles.title: Truco para abrir un menú secreto en iPhone y Android: desde WhatsApp hasta Call of Dutty
articles.text:
Los teléfonos iPhone y Android esconden funciones que pueden ahorrar varios pasos al utilizar aplicaciones cotidianas. Una de ellas aparece al mantener pulsado el icono de una aplicación en la pantalla de inicio, un gesto que abre un menú contextual con accesos directos a algunas de sus funciones más utilizadas.
Este menú está disponible en buena parte de las aplicaciones, aunque las opciones dependen de cada desarrollador. En servicios como WhatsApp puede permitir iniciar rápidamente un nuevo chat o acceder a contactos frecuentes, mientras que en navegadores puede ofrecer la posibilidad de abrir una pestaña de incógnito.
PUBLICIDAD
En algunos videojuegos, como Call of Duty, también pueden aparecer accesos directos relacionados con el inicio del juego u otras funciones.
Cómo abrir el menú oculto de las aplicaciones
El procedimiento es prácticamente idéntico en los dos principales sistemas operativos móviles. No es necesario instalar aplicaciones adicionales ni modificar ninguna configuración del teléfono.
Para utilizarlo, solo hay que localizar el icono de la aplicación en la pantalla de inicio y mantenerlo presionado durante un par de segundos. En ese momento aparecerá un pequeño menú con diferentes acciones disponibles.
PUBLICIDAD
Después, basta con tocar la función que se quiera utilizar para ejecutarla directamente. De esta manera, el usuario puede saltarse varios pasos que normalmente tendría que realizar después de abrir la aplicación.
El gesto también sirve para reorganizar los iconos. Si, después de mantener pulsado el acceso directo, se continúa arrastrando el dedo, es posible mover la aplicación a otra posición de la pantalla de inicio.
PUBLICIDAD
WhatsApp, navegadores y otras aplicaciones
La utilidad de este menú depende de las funciones que cada desarrollador haya decidido incorporar. Por eso, no todas las aplicaciones ofrecen las mismas posibilidades.
En WhatsApp, por ejemplo, el menú contextual puede incluir accesos rápidos para comenzar una nueva conversación o abrir chats con contactos utilizados con frecuencia. Esto permite iniciar una conversación sin entrar primero a la aplicación y buscar posteriormente la opción correspondiente.
PUBLICIDAD
Los navegadores también pueden aprovechar este sistema para ofrecer accesos directos. Entre ellos puede encontrarse la apertura de una nueva pestaña, una ventana de navegación privada o determinadas funciones habituales del navegador.
En otras aplicaciones pueden aparecer opciones completamente diferentes. Por ello, una forma sencilla de descubrir estos accesos es mantener pulsados los iconos de las aplicaciones que más se utilizan y revisar las acciones disponibles.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo guardar un acceso directo en Android
Android ofrece una posibilidad adicional para aprovechar estos menús. Si una aplicación muestra un acceso directo especialmente útil, el usuario puede mantener pulsada esa acción concreta y arrastrarla hasta la pantalla de inicio.
De esta manera, la función queda convertida en un acceso directo independiente. En lugar de mantener pulsado el icono de la aplicación cada vez, basta con tocar el nuevo acceso para ejecutar directamente esa tarea.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta opción resulta especialmente práctica cuando una función determinada se utiliza con frecuencia y se quieren reducir los pasos necesarios para acceder a ella.
Qué ocurre en un iPhone
En iOS, el funcionamiento es ligeramente diferente cuando se quiere reorganizar la pantalla. Al mantener pulsado el icono aparece primero el menú contextual con las acciones disponibles.
PUBLICIDAD
Para utilizar una de ellas, basta con tocarla. Sin embargo, si se continúa manteniendo el dedo sobre la pantalla, el sistema puede entrar en el modo de edición del escritorio, en el que los iconos comienzan a moverse y pueden cambiarse de posición o eliminarse.
Por ello, conviene distinguir entre mantener pulsado brevemente para consultar las funciones rápidas y continuar presionando para modificar la pantalla de inicio.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: GitHub Hardens npm and Actions Defaults, Drawing Debate over Delays versus Signing
articles.text:
GitHub has consolidated the changes it shipped across npm and GitHub Actions between March and July 2026 to disrupt supply chain attacks. Nothing in the post is new, since every item already landed through the changelog; however, it makes clear how many of these changes alter defaults rather than add options.
Greg Ose, principal product security engineer, and Zachary Steindler, principal software engineer, frame the problem as one without a single fix. These attacks chain several weaknesses together, so GitHub has prioritized the mitigations that break the most impactful links.
For initial compromise, npm now places high-impact accounts into read-only mode for 72 hours when they change their email address or use a 2FA recovery code. On the Actions side, the default behavior of actions/checkout changed so workflows no longer check out untrusted fork code under commonly exploited triggers unless a team explicitly opts out. That change was backported, so it reaches pipelines that pinned an earlier release.
Two further controls target escalation. Workflow execution policies let admins govern who may trigger workflows and which trigger types are permitted, while the Actions cache is now read-only for untrusted triggers, closing the path where an attacker poisons a shared cache entry to reach privileged release workflows.
For credential exfiltration, the guidance is blunt: removing long-lived credentials from the pipeline is the single most effective step, and npm trusted publishing now supports CircleCI. An Actions network firewall is in technical preview, logging outbound traffic so teams can spot unusual destinations.
On propagation, npm staged publishing holds versions until an additional approval and 2FA step completes, and npm v12 disables install scripts by default along with dependencies fetched via git or remote URLs. Dependabot version updates now wait three days before opening a pull request.
Community reactions on Hacker News have been sharply divided, centering less on the individual controls than on whether time delays are the right instrument at all.
The 72-hour account freeze drew immediate argument over how the number was chosen. As one commenter, datakan, put it, maintainers travel and take leave, and attacks are often timed for Fridays precisely because nobody is watching:
There is a big difference between 3 days when someone may be sick or traveling and not looking and 30, which aligns better with 99% of scenarios this may be an issue with. 3 days is absurd. Even password apps with kill switches will default to 7 days.
Others rejected the premise that a single correct value exists. Every longer number invites a longer one, and a month-long publishing block would require an override path that does not currently exist. Commenter Normal_gaussian proposed the empirical version: plot compromised repositories against the time a maintainer takes to begin resolution, and pick a value just past the inflection point.
A sharper objection came from lrvick, who described buying the expired email domain of a sole npm package author for eight dollars, putting the ability to ship code to roughly 70,000 companies within reach of a password reset:
72 hours would not make a difference here.
He extended that into the thread's dominant critique, that the industry keeps building process gates while declining to implement author-side package signing of the kind Linux distributions have had since the 1990s, and that npm has rejected pull requests implementing it, even optionally, for a decade.
The rebuttal came from acdha, who argued that what actually keeps Linux distributions safer is fewer people with push access combined with a time delay, rather than signatures as such:
What keeps Linux distributions safer is that fewer people are able to push updates and there’s a time delay. The compromises are because people exploit release pipelines, and if your build infrastructure is compromised, it’ll merrily sign the compromised packages as well.
Commenter summarybot framed the cooldown approach as an admission of failure, given that GitHub owns npm and has extensive code analysis capability:
Introducing a cooldown period seems like the lowest tech solution to a technological problem I have seen in a long while.
The counterargument from insanitybit was operational: cooldowns do not depend on updating detection rules or keeping pace with obfuscation, and they buy scanners time to do their work.
Trusted publishing generated the most practical exchange, prompted by a question about why it helps when an attacker has already compromised the workflow. As commenter pimterry explained:
Trusted staged publishing helps a lot: you have to independently pwn the workflow _and_ then complete a separate 2FA flow as a maintainer. The workflow never sees any keys that can publish independently.
Others added that the attacker must trigger the specific workflow, which leaves a trace on GitHub.
If these reactions are representative, the disagreement is not about whether the individual controls help but about what they substitute for. GitHub has chosen mechanisms that work without maintainer participation, while the mechanism practitioners keep asking for, author-side signing, requires exactly that participation and has been declined for a decade on the grounds that it would deter contributors.
The asymmetry worth noting is that the changes arriving automatically are the moderate ones, while the strongest protections, staged and trusted publishing, remain opt-in and unevenly adopted. The install-script change in npm v12 will also break builds that never audited what runs at install time.
The changes are rolling out now, with GitHub pointing to its changelog for the remainder.

articles.title: We tested the impact of SSD speed on gaming performance in 11 titles — we analyzed from SATA to PCIe 5.0 to see whether upgrading to a faster NVMe SSD would have an impact
articles.text:
We tested the impact of SSD speed on gaming performance in 11 titles — we analyzed from SATA to PCIe 5.0 to see whether upgrading to a faster NVMe SSD would have an impact
NVMe or SATA, or either?
We tested gaming performance with both NVMe and SATA SSDs across 11 games to determine if upgrading to a faster drive is worth it. Solid-state drives (SSDs) have been a staple of PC gaming for years, but their importance grew significantly with the launch of the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S in 2020. Both consoles feature high-speed NVMe SSDs and storage architectures designed to fully leverage their capabilities, enabling faster asset streaming and reducing traditional storage bottlenecks.
As a result, game developers have increasingly developed their titles for SSDs, with many modern games now listing them as a minimum system requirement. But how exactly do games use SSDs during gameplay, and does upgrading to a faster SSD actually improve gaming performance? In this article, we'll examine SSD activity in modern games and determine whether higher storage speeds translate into a better gaming experience. Given the surge in SSD prices, will a slower drive deliver comparable gaming performance to high-end alternatives?
Load Times
Load Times
While this article focuses primarily on SSD activity and performance during gameplay, loading times remain one of the most significant advantages of solid-state storage. It's well known that games can take several minutes to load from an HDD, whereas modern SSDs typically reduce load times to just a few seconds.
The gap between SSDs is much smaller. In some titles, PCIe NVMe drives can load games several times faster than SATA SSDs, but in many cases, the difference is relatively small. Naturally, different generations of PCIe SSDs have even smaller differences, with flagship drives often delivering only marginal improvements to loading times despite their substantially higher sequential throughput.
Disk I/O Operations in Games
Disk I/O Operations in Games
Before examining the performance results, it's important to understand the types of disk I/O operations that games typically generate. Two key metrics are block size and queue depth. The block size of an I/O operation defines the size of the chunk of data a game will read at one time, while queue depth is the number of pending I/O requests that a storage device has queued at any one time.
During gameplay, the vast majority of storage activity consists of random read operations as game assets are streamed from storage into memory. Sequential reads are less common, and write activity is generally minimal.
Microsoft provides several storage optimization recommendations for developers in its DirectStorage documentation. Although these guidelines are intended for DirectStorage-enabled titles, many of the underlying principles apply to games in general, even if they do not use DirectStorage. Among Microsoft's recommendations are the use of block sizes of at least 32k and sufficiently high queue depths to maximize storage throughput.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Modern games typically employ 32k or 64k random I/O requests. However, despite Microsoft's recommendations, most games continue to operate at relatively low queue depths.
Performance Comparison
Performance Comparison
Now we will examine SSD activity and compare performance across different SSD generations. The games included in our testing were selected because they either exhibited higher storage bandwidth than usual, had greater peak or average SSD utilization, had support for DirectStorage, or because they are popular titles that many gamers would be interested in seeing analyzed from a storage-performance perspective.
To place as much stress as possible on each SSD, all testing was conducted with 16GB of system memory. Using a smaller memory capacity reduces the amount of game data that can be held in RAM, forcing games to rely more heavily on the SSD than they would in a 64GB configuration. It also better reflects the configurations found in many mainstream gaming PCs. That said, we observed little difference in SSD activity when comparing 16GB and 64GB memory configurations.
When interpreting the SSD activity data below, it is important to understand that 100% utilization does not necessarily mean an SSD is reaching its maximum rated bandwidth. For example, a PCIe 4.0 SSD reporting 100% utilization is unlikely to be delivering its full 7.5 GB/s of sequential read throughput. In gaming workloads, SSDs can become fully utilized while transferring data at significantly lower bandwidths.
This is because the speeds advertised by SSD manufacturers are based on sequential read performance, whereas games primarily rely on random reads. While random-read throughput can approach sequential-read speeds under certain conditions, doing so requires sufficiently large block sizes and high queue depths. Although modern games often use relatively large block sizes, they typically do not use the high queue depths needed to fully saturate an SSD's theoretical bandwidth.
We have also chosen not to test any traditional hard drive disks. There are many documented examples of modern games performing poorly, taking an unbearably long time to load, or having visual issues when installing the game on an HDD. There are some games where this may not be an issue, but we still do not recommend playing modern games on an HDD.
The testing was conducted in gameplay. No built-in benchmarks were used. We found that SSD activity increases with higher settings, so that is where we focused our testing. We set each game to its absolute maximum settings.
We used HWiNFO to measure SSD activity and set it to the lowest polling rate possible to capture activity accurately without incurring overhead.
Test system
- MSI GeForce RTX 5090 Vanguard SOC
- Ryzen 7 9800X3D
- 16GB G.Skill Trident Z5 DDR5 6000 MHz CL30
- Crucial T700 Gen5 SSD
- Sabrent Rocket 4 Plus-G Gen4 SSD
- Adata XPG SX8200 Pro Gen3 SSD
- Samsung 870 EVO SATA III SSD
- Asus ROG Strix B850-F Gaming WiFi
- Corsair Nautilus 360 RS AIO Cooler
- MSI MPG Ai1600TS PCIe 5 PSU
- HAGS enabled
- Windows 11 25H2 (Build 26200.8737)
- Nvidia driver 610.62
Forspoken
Forspoken
Forspoken was the first game to support DirectStorage on PC. DirectStorage is a feature that aims to allow games to make full use of high-speed storage devices while reducing the CPU overhead associated with making reads from disk.
Looking at the table below, you can see that it does exhibit a fairly high peak and average bandwidth. In fact, it’s the highest average bandwidth we have seen in any game we have tested. Average utilization is also quite high, and the game hits 100% SSD utilization frequently.
| SSD Activity at 1080p |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | Peak Bandwidth | Average Bandwidth | Peak Utilization | Average Utilization | 
| SATA SSD | 485 MB/s | 240 MB/s | 100% | 52% | 
| PCIe 3.0 | 1324 MB/s | 301 MB/s | 100% | 50% | 
| PCIe 4.0 | 2956 MB/s | 374 MB/s | 100% | 30% | 
| PCIe 5.0 | 2761 MB/s | 307 MB/s | 100% | 19% | 
| SSD Activity at 1440p |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | Peak Bandwidth | Average Bandwidth | Peak Utilization | Average Utilization |

| PCIe 3.0 | 1645 MB/s | 318 MB/s | 100% | 56% | 
| PCIe 4.0 | 2931 MB/s | 382 MB/s | 100% | 28% | 
| PCIe 5.0 | 2890 MB/s | 352 MB/s | 100% | 17% | 
| SSD Activity at 2160p |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | Peak Bandwidth | Average Bandwidth | Peak Utilization | Average Utilization |

| PCIe 4.0 | 2886 MB/s | 379 MB/s | 100% | 26% | 
| PCIe 5.0 | 2901 MB/s | 366 MB/s | 100% | 19% | 
How does this translate to performance?
While there is no difference in performance between the PCIe NVMe SSDs, you can see that having a PCIe SSD can give you a large boost in the 1% lows compared to a SATA SSD. We see a 39% increase in 1% lows at 4K, a 51% increase at 1440p, and a 22% increase at 1080p.
The higher peak and average bandwidth used by the PCIe drives resulted in higher 1% lows in this game, which makes for a smoother gameplay experience.
Alan Wake 2
Alan Wake 2
Alan Wake 2 makes extensive use of modern rendering technologies, including path tracing, mesh shaders, and RTX Mega Geometry. In a recent interview, Remedy explained that the game operates with a fixed memory budget, continuously streaming the assets required for the current scene from the SSD while evicting assets that are no longer needed. This approach keeps memory usage under control despite the game's highly detailed textures and geometry, making Alan Wake 2 one of the most storage-intensive titles available today.
| SSD Activity at 1080p |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  | Peak Bandwidth | Average Bandwidth | Peak Utilization | Average Utilization | 
| SATA SSD | 562 MB/s | 80 MB/s | 100% | 63% | 
| PCIe 3.0 | 582 MB/s | 83 MB/s | 100% | 62% | 
| PCIe 4.0 | 572 MB/s | 82 MB/s | 91% | 14% |

|  | Peak Bandwidth | Average Bandwidth | Peak Utilization | Average Utilization | 
| SATA SSD | 570 MB/s | 100 MB/s | 100% | 72% | 
| PCIe 3.0 | 938 MB/s | 113 MB/s | 100% | 62% | 
| PCIe 4.0 | 887 MB/s | 111 MB/s | 100% | 19% | 
| PCIe 5.0 | 1673 MB/s | 116 MB/s | 100% | 17% | 
| SSD Activity at 2160p |  |  |  |  |

The SSD activity increases with resolution in this game. We see an average of over 200 MB/s on each drive at 4K, which is rare for a game. We also see a whopping 5.1 GB/s of peak bandwidth on a PCIe 5.0 SSD at 4K.
How does this impact performance?
Unlike Forspoken, we do not see any difference in performance here for any of the drives tested.
Although the faster SSDs reach higher peak bandwidth, these peaks are only brief bursts rather than sustained transfers. In other words, the game is not continuously streaming multiple gigabytes of data every second. Instead, it transfers smaller amounts of data over very short intervals, resulting in high instantaneous bandwidth readings. As a result, the average bandwidth is the more meaningful metric, and it remains relatively similar across all of the SSDs we tested.
The average utilization on the SATA SSD can reach over 80% at 4K, but it is not enough to degrade its performance in comparison to the PCIe drives.
Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart
Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart
| SSD Activity at 1080p |  |  |  |  |

| PCIe 5.0 | 2234 MB/s | 64 MB/s | 57% | 2% | 
The disk bandwidth through this sequence is actually lower than the previous two games. This makes sense, as the game uses GPU decompression, which increases the effective bandwidth flowing through the PCIe bus beyond what CPU decompression would. However, this increase in effective bandwidth is not reflected in the data that is being read from disk.
When reading the performance charts below, it is important to note that PCIe SSDs reduce portal transition times by roughly 2-3 seconds compared to SATA SSDs. On SATA drives, Ratchet therefore spends more time within each portal sequence. As a result, average performance and 1% lows can generally be slightly higher on SATA SSDs, since there is less active rendering during these extended transition periods. However, there is one exception.
While the SATA SSD has an advantage at 1440p and 1080p due to the extended time spent inside of each portal, the 1% lows take a hit at 4K. The SATA drive does not handle the first portal transition in the sequence particularly well at 4K, and so the PCIe drives have about a 38% advantage in 1% lows.
This portal sequence is the most storage-intensive part of the game. In normal gameplay, the game uses significantly less bandwidth, and so there is no difference in performance at all between the SATA SSD and the PCIe SSDs.
Spider-Man 2
Spider-Man 2
Spider-Man 2 was the second game to use GPU decompression of assets on PC. This is the third DirectStorage title we have tested so far.

Since the game uses GPU decompression, the effective bandwidth after decompression will be considerably higher than what we see here, but none of the SSDs we tested are being stressed in this game.
Performance is virtually identical on all drives in this game.
Starfield
Starfield
Starfield is an open world game that constantly reads data from disk. It also frequently hits 100% disk utilization as you traverse the world.

In previous games, 100% SSD utilization was accompanied by much higher peak bandwidth. Here, the lower peak bandwidth suggests the game uses a very low queue depth for its read operations. As you move through the open world, it continuously streams data from the SSD in frequent, small transfers, keeping average bandwidth very low.
Once again, we see no improvement in performance going from the SATA SSD to any of the faster PCIe NVME SSDs.
DOOM: The Dark Ages
DOOM: The Dark Ages
DOOM: The Dark Ages was the first game to list an NVMe SSD as a requirement. Not only is it listed as such on the PC system requirements, but Bethesda has a support page that reiterates that installing the game on an NVMe SSD is required.
The developers at idSoftware mentioned that the game uses a proprietary ultra-fast continuous sector streaming tech that virtually eliminates load times between levels.

The drives we tested are hardly being stressed in DOOM: The Dark Ages.
Given the disk utilization figures, it comes as no surprise that all of the tested drives deliver identical gameplay performance.
Although this article focuses on in-game performance rather than loading times, we also found little difference in load times when using a SATA SSD. Loading screens were not noticeably longer, and we observed no visual artifacts or streaming issues while playing on the slower drive.
Based on our testing, it is unclear why Bethesda lists an NVMe SSD as a requirement. A SATA SSD provided an indistinguishable gameplay experience, with no measurable performance drawbacks or observable streaming issues.
Dead Space Remake
Dead Space Remake
Dead Space Remake made headlines when it launched with abhorrent performance and stuttering issues. But how much of that was due to streaming from slower storage? Does a faster SSD help performance?

Although average disk utilization and bandwidth are relatively low, the game frequently reaches 100% utilization. Yet even during these periods, peak bandwidth remains well below what PCIe SSDs can achieve under high-queue-depth random workloads. This indicates the game is issuing read requests at a very low queue depth, leaving much of the SSD's available performance untapped. Additionally, the difference in average bandwidth between the SSDs is minimal.
All drives provide the same performance. There is nothing to be gained from a faster SSD in this title.
Cyberpunk 2077
Cyberpunk 2077
We included Cyberpunk 2077 in our testing because the game features a large and seamless open world, and it is one of the most popular games ever released.

The average bandwidth is by far the lowest we have seen in the games tested so far. This is not entirely surprising. Although the game was released in the same year as the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, development began well before those consoles were released. As a cross-generation title, it also needed to run on the previous generation of consoles, which relied on mechanical hard drives. As a result, the game's streaming system was designed to perform well on significantly slower storage devices.
There is no noticeable difference in performance across the drives tested.
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered

007 First Light

F1 25

The game exhibits higher peak and average bandwidth than many of the games we have tested, but it is still not enough to truly stress a SATA SSD.
Once more, all of the drives show identical performance.
What About the Visuals?
What About the Visuals?
Many readers may be wondering if playing on a SATA drive resulted in any visual anomalies, such as slower loading textures, additional pop-in, or other visual artifacts. We did not notice any such issues in the 11 games we tested. There are some games that exhibit pop-in, but that is consistent across all storage devices. All of the drives we used in our testing provided an identical visual experience.
The Verdict
The Verdict
Out of all the games tested, only two showed measurable performance differences between SATA and PCIe SSDs: Forspoken and Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart.
In Forspoken, moving from a SATA SSD to any PCIe SSD – regardless of generation – resulted in a significant improvement in 1% lows.
Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart showed more nuanced results. During the portal sequences at 1440p and 1080p, average framerate and 1% lows were slightly higher on the SATA SSD, as slower loading increased the time spent inside the portals. Since the portals contain less on-screen complexity, framerates are naturally higher within them. However, at 4K resolution, PCIe SSDs delivered better 1% lows. Outside of the portal sequence in normal gameplay, there was no measurable performance difference between any of the drives.
Across all other titles, PCIe SSDs provided no meaningful performance advantage, and there were no observable differences between PCIe generations. In the vast majority of games tested, a SATA SSD delivers comparable performance.

articles.title: Working hard or hardly working? More than half of workers have sent unneeded emails or messages just to show they are doing something
articles.text:
Working hard or hardly working? More than half of workers have sent unneeded emails or messages just to show they are doing something
Click reply to prove you’re profitable
- 52% of workers have sent replies to message or emails simply to prove that they are working
- Focused work is being interrupted by the requirement to respond quickly, with response speeds raised in performance evaluations
- More than half have replied at weekends, evenings, or even on annual leave to remain available and accessible
Are you staying in touch with your boss? New research suggests that career performance is being silently evaluated by speedy responses and availability, alongside traditional metrics, and this is resulting in employees interrupting focused work to reassure their managers.
A Use.AI survey of 15,842 adults across the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and Latin America has found that 68% of employees believe that replying quickly demonstrates a higher level of commitment than slower colleagues.
There could be an AI element to this, too, with respondents who work extensively with AI feeling that response expectations are higher than those who have less exposure or requirement for the technology.
Fastest fingers first
The results from the survey strongly suggest that managers and team leaders are demanding fast responses, but that this doesn’t necessarily have the desired outcome.
For example, focused work has been interrupted by 48% of those surveyed in order to check emails or messages that might require an urgent response. Meanwhile, more than half (53%) have replied at weekends, evenings, or even on annual leave to remain available and accessible to their line managers.
Perhaps the most surprising result from the survey is that 52% say they have sent unnecessary messages or made changes to their status in messaging tools purely to demonstrate that they are working.
The new demands on employees have not gone unnoticed nor unmentioned. 42% have found themselves discussing their speediness in responding to messages in performance meetings.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Curiously, despite completing work in a timely manner, 29% have been “criticized” for slow responses to messages, highlighting a curious conflict in communication.
Is AI inflating expectations?
The survey also explores the matter of how artificial intelligence tools are impacting workplace expectations. Here, it found that 62% who use AI widely have found expected response times to emails had decreased. Conversely, just 38% of those will less regular AI use noted the same change.
While this doesn’t mean that AI caused that change, the results may suggest that the introduction of AI isn’t just impacting workflows and productivity. Enhanced, smarter systems underpinned by LLMs and agentic solutions are introducing an unforeseen tension, a mistrust from management concerning employees’ ability to devote time to work.
“AI is making routine communication almost effortless, but that convenience is also compressing expectations around response times,” said Use.AI’s Co-Founder and CEO, Ihor Herasymov. “We risk mistaking responsiveness for productivity.”
Fast responses to emails and messages may signal attentiveness, does this necessarily tally with solid results?

articles.title: Alternativas a Duolingo para aprender idiomas de forma práctica, inmersiva y divertida
articles.text:
Duolingo es posiblemente una de las aplicaciones más populares. La hayas usado o no. Prueba de ello es la cantidad de memes que protagoniza en internet. Y tiene el mérito de haber popularizado el método de aprender idiomas jugando. Con pequeñas píldoras de conocimiento fáciles de digerir cuando solo tienes unos pocos minutos. Sin embargo, con el paso de los años, muchos han visto que su método no es del todo eficaz. Y que hay que acompañarlo de otras actividades más tradicionales si quieres leer, escribir, hablar y, en definitiva, manejarte con un idioma. En este sentido, han proliferado multitud de alternativas a Duolingo. Algunas imitando su estilo. Y otras con propuestas dispares.
Puede que la inteligencia artificial sea capaz de traducir textos y audios en tiempo real. Pero eso no impide que todavía sea necesario aprender idiomas si quieres entender a más gente, ampliar tus posibilidades laborales o, simplemente, ampliar tus horizontes culturales. Lo bueno es que tienes muchas herramientas para hacerlo posible. Incluso con IA. Y compatibles entre sí. Como, por ejemplo, ver películas y series en versión original, escuchar música en ese idioma que quieres aprender o hablar con nativos de esa lengua que se te resiste.
Y todo eso lo puedes combinar con aplicaciones alternativas a Duolingo. Siempre es buen momento para dedicarle unos minutos a juegos y actividades relacionadas con aprender idiomas a base de repetir conceptos, palabras y expresiones. Veamos qué proponen las siguientes aplicaciones para aprender idiomas y olvidarte del búho verde que tan pesado se pone cuando dejas de atenderlo durante unos días.
Drops
Empezamos por Drops. Palabra que en inglés significa gotas y que hace referencia al método que emplean hoy en día muchas aplicaciones para aprender idiomas, programación o cualquier área de conocimiento que implique dedicar horas, días, semanas, meses o años. Vamos, el divide y vencerás de toda la vida. Como curiosidad, Drops es propiedad de Kahoot!, empresa que se hizo popular por su herramienta para crear juegos interactivos que utilizan escuelas e institutos de medio mundo. Y que hoy cuenta con otras muchas aplicaciones educativas para distintas edades.
Drops ofrece más de 50 idiomas para que los aprendas, uno por uno, a poder ser. El método te sonará: realizar pequeñas actividades a modo de juegos con cuestionarios, preguntas y respuestas y todos los elementos necesarios para motivarte a seguir aprendiendo con esta alternativa a Duolingo. Y todas las actividades van enfocadas a situaciones prácticas que puedes encontrarte en un viaje, en el trabajo o en otros momentos de tu día a día. El objetivo, que aprendas las 5.000 palabras más utilizadas en ese idioma. Y, para motivarte, pegatinas, barras de progreso, niveles y otras fruslerías.
Como es habitual en este tipo de aplicaciones para aprender idiomas, Drops es gratuita, aunque si vas a exprimirla al máximo, tal vez tengas que pagar una suscripción, que puedes probar gratis durante una semana. Por lo demás, puedes descargarla en iOS y en Android.
Mondly
Otra alternativa a Duolingo a tener en cuenta es Mondly. Cuenta con más de 40 idiomas para aprender “en cualquier momento, en cualquier lugar, en cualquier dispositivo”. Disponible para iOS, para Android y en formato Web, también se basa en el método de simplificar el aprendizaje reduciéndolo a lecciones imprescindibles que pueden darse durante unos minutos del día a día. En total, 50 temas para memorizar palabras y expresiones que necesitarás en momentos puntuales y habituales si viajas, trabajas o, simplemente, te relacionas con otras personas.
A las lecciones temáticas de Mondly hay que añadir decenas de conversaciones que debes recrear, por escrito o hablando, con ayuda de la IA. Y que te permitirán practicar lo aprendido. Por lo demás, Mondly combina el modelo gratuito con una versión de pago más amplia. Gratis, tienes acceso a las lecciones diarias y a los retos semanales y mensuales. Y si quieres desbloquear todas las lecciones, las conversaciones y la revisión de vocabulario, en ese caso tendrás que pagar por la suscripción. Que puede ser mensual, trimestral o anual. Como el gimnasio.
Clozemaster
Una frase cada vez. Clozemaster es una alternativa a Duolingo que se define directamente como “un juego en el que mejoras tus habilidades lingüísticas completando la palabra que falta para miles de oraciones”. En vez de lanzarte píldoras con palabras que se repiten en los minijuegos, apuesta por enseñarte las 10.000 palabras más populares del idioma que vas a aprender mediante frases que debes completar. Así aprendes la palabra por contexto y, de paso, frases en las que usar esa palabra. Para cuando llegue el momento de ponerla en práctica.
Con más de 50 lenguas en su catálogo, Clozemaster te permite aprender idiomas de manera reposada y con un entorno minimalista. De acuerdo, conserva los elementos clásicos de Duolingo, como los puntos, las barras de progreso y otros parámetros cuantificables, pero se diferencia de las demás alternativas a Duolingo en que es un proyecto más sobrio y que va directo al grano. Aunque eso no exime que sea gratuito con una versión de pago con suscripción para quienes busquen desbloquear todas sus funciones.
Busuu
Cuando Duolingo llegó con sus juegos de repetición de palabras, Busuu ya estaba allí. Esta veterana aplicación para aprender idiomas es una de las alternativas a Duolingo más longevas. Su principal baza es que te conecta con otros usuarios, creando una comunidad de personas que aprenden y que ayudan a otros a aprender. De manera que, además de los clásicos juegos y actividades para aprender palabras, conceptos y expresiones, puedes poner en práctica lo aprendido escribiendo textos o conversando con otras personas.
Busuu te da “acceso a lecciones compactas de los expertos y conéctate con una comunidad de hablantes nativos para ayudarte a dominar las palabras más rápido”. De manera que podrás combinar el estilo Duolingo con el contacto humano, aunque virtual, de hablantes en ese idioma que quieres aprender. Y, de momento, tanto los cursos y lecciones como el acceso a la comunidad son gratuitos.
La parte de pago de Busuu incluye conversaciones con IA, por si te da reparo hablar con personas, actividades de pronunciación, revisión profesional de gramática y vocabulario, certificados propios de haber aprendido un idioma, modo offline, etc. Vamos, que puedes pasarte el juego gratis y, si quieres más, pagar solo si tú quieres. Por lo demás, puedes usar Busuu desde su web, desde iOS y desde Android.
Memrise
No podemos terminar esta lista de alternativas a Duolingo sin Memrise, la propuesta para aprender idiomas que combina vídeos de hablantes nativos, ejercicios de vocabulario, comprensión oral e inteligencia artificial para ayudarte a aprender una lengua de una forma práctica y cotidiana. Como reza en su página oficial, quiere ayudarte a “pasar un examen, progresar en el trabajo, construir relaciones o, simplemente, mantener tu mente fresca”.
Como las aplicaciones anteriores, no importa qué nivel tengas. Puedes aprender un idioma desde cero de una lista extensa. También ampliar vocabulario, mejorar tu comprensión oral con videos, practicar conversaciones y, en definitiva, cubrir el idioma leído, escrito, hablado y oído. Y, siguiendo las demás alternativas a Duolingo, usar esta app no te llevará más de 10 o 15 minutos al día.
A diferencia de Duolingo y otras apps, Memrise ofrece un aspecto más serio, aunque eso no impide que emplee las mismas prácticas de motivarte con actividades, juegos, progresos y niveles. Y como aliciente, te permite practicar pruebas de cara a aprobar exámenes oficiales. Por último, Memrise sigue también la tradición de ser gratuita, aunque con funciones de pago para los más exigentes. Y, cómo no, la tienes disponible en iOS y en Android.

articles.title: La conduite autonome au second plan : cette option est la préférée des conducteurs
articles.text:
Les commerciaux automobiles ont du boulot. Pour vendre la voiture, c’est sûr, mais également pour organiser la mise en main du véhicule à sa livraison. L’automobiliste lambda n’a aucune chance de connaître tous les équipements de son auto flambant neuve. Il faut donc tout lui apprendre, pas à pas. Étant donné que les voitures sont de plus en plus équipées, ce processus prend de plus en plus de temps…
Un calvaire pour les commerciaux : quand les voitures deviennent trop complexes
Tout cela pour au final n’utiliser qu’une maigre fraction des équipements de son véhicule ! Un gâchis ? Pas réellement… Il faudrait plutôt cibler l’apprentissage sur ce qui plaît le plus aux automobilistes. Cela tombe à pic, le cabinet américain AutoPacific a mené une étude sur 19 000 clients potentiels. L’enquête portait sur l’équipement le plus réclamé, et donc normalement le plus utilisé dans leur futur véhicule.
Le siège chauffant grand vainqueur
Lequel arriverait en premier, selon vous ? La conduite semi-autonome, n’est-ce pas ? Eh bien pas du tout ! Le système ne parvient même pas à se glisser sur le podium des fonctionnalités les plus demandées. L’équipement favori est le siège chauffant, réclamé par 47 % des interrogés. Extrêmement commode en hiver, mais bien moins utile en ce moment… En seconde place se trouve un ensemble dont l’utilisation ne dépend aucunement des saisons.
L’aide au stationnement et le freinage d’urgence : les nouveaux indispensables
Il s’agit de l’aide au stationnement, aujourd’hui devenue indispensable vu l’inflation généralisée de la taille des véhicules couplée à une visibilité périphérique de plus en plus réduite. Pas étonnant alors qu’il s’agisse d’un must-have pour 45 % des sondés. Juste derrière vient la suite logique, le freinage d’urgence en marche arrière permettant d’éviter les bobos à basse vitesse.
Du siège électrique au chargeur à induction : le classement complet des favoris
Si cet équipement est réclamé par 44 % des intéressés, nous le trouvons particulièrement insupportable, celui-ci freinant pour un rien. Ensuite viennent à égalité le siège conducteur électrique, l’assistance au changement de voie, la vision nocturne, la conduite semi-autonome et la caméra d’angle mort. Ces cinq systèmes sont les favoris de 43 % des interrogés. L’alerte de circulation transversale en marche arrière se place juste derrière, avec 42 % des faveurs.
Parking automatique, dashcam, détection d’animaux : intéressants mais pas indispensables
Le parking automatique et le chargeur à induction pour smartphones sont à égalité en étant cités par 41 % des personnes. Même histoire pour le siège passager électrique et la caméra embarquée, la fameuse dashcam, tous deux choisis par 40 % des sondés. Enfin, le système de détection des animaux et la transmission intégrale sont aussi au coude à coude, avec 39 % des préférences.

articles.title: Dropbox is a PC builder’s best friend
articles.text:
In 2018 I bet my reputation and self-worth on a huge crowdfunded game design project. It could have been a failure for many reasons, but the one I became most worried about was losing all of the work that was stored locally on my home-built PC — a scenario that would have left a lot of people very upset and placed me in deep trouble. I wasn’t irresponsible, I had local backups, but at some point I found myself in custody of so many important files that it scared me. And no matter how many redundancies I could build at home, they’d all still be in the same place — a risky bet. So I bought a subscription to Dropbox. Years later, it’s still one of the best software subscriptions that I happily renew each year.
Dropbox is a PC builder’s best friend
When catastrophe strikes, having your whole computer in the cloud makes recovery a breeze.
It was great to have all that work backed up in the cloud — both for peace of mind and because it made working with collaborators breezier, letting them upload stuff directly to my drive, and letting me transfer files up to 50GB in size. In quick order I had built a trove of incredible artwork and complicated InDesign, Photoshop, and Illustrator files. The original goal for my Dropbox configuration was to make sure I wouldn’t lose any data in a worst-case scenario, so I set it up to mirror everything living on my work partition. Eventually, I ran smack into a worst-case scenario. Not once, but twice.
I’m still not sure why, but my latest home-built PC chewed through two separate 2TB Samsung 970 Evo SSDs. It’s difficult to tell what went wrong with them, but in each case I woke up one morning to find when I tried to boot up that no drive could be detected. I can still feel my stomach trying to sink into the floor when I press that power button these days, never knowing if my drive had died in its sleep.
Fortunately, both times, after some process-of-elimination testing I learned that just the drive had gone bad and everything else in my system was A-OK. Maybe I should have ditched Samsung after the second disaster, but I’m now on an 2TB 990 Evo Plus. Knock on wood, this thing better not fail. That drive now costs almost twice what I originally paid for it thanks to our new outrageously priced world of parts.
My Dropbox bill is about $204 a year for a family plan ($17 a month), which includes up to six members. If you’re just in it for yourself you can get it for $9.99 a month billed yearly (about $120 a year), which comes with 2TB of storage. You can upgrade to 3TB for around $143 a year. That might be a tough sell for people who already have dozens of subscriptions, but I find it to be a decent price for excellent digital insurance.
There are other powerful options out there, especially for professionals working with heavy files or complicated workflows. Backblaze, for example, has a personal backup plan with unlimited data for $99 a year and no restrictions on file size. And, of course, if you live on the Mac, Apple iCloud Plus isn’t a bad option — especially if you’re already paying for an Apple One subscription. Even Adobe offers file backups through Creative Cloud if that’s your jam, but I would not recommend using that clunky software suite for anything other than doing the work you need to do.
I can’t recall a single time the service failed
I prefer Dropbox because the software works consistently well across multiple operating systems and is usually neither seen nor heard. The Windows client is snappy and I’ve found with a fast internet connection that its real-time syncing is efficient and painless. Anytime a file is modified in the partition I have mirrored in the cloud, Dropbox quietly begins uploading it and making changes to my mirrored files in the cloud. After using it for about eight years now I can’t recall a single time the service failed or faltered. It’s so fast and reliable I often forget it’s even there.
Now, for the important caveat: This might not work for you if you have poor internet speeds. It really depends on how much data you’re regularly moving around on your computer and how quickly you make changes to it. This could particularly be a problem for asymmetrical data plans that commonly boast lightning-fast download speeds while offering pathetic upload speeds. I’ve done fine averaging only about 20Mbps upload, but if you’re on something even lower you should try a free trial for a backup plan before committing. You can also find plenty of download time calculators online; at my gigabit download speed it usually takes around two hours to download the 1TB of files I have synced in the cloud.
And one more caveat: Putting everything (or even just many things) on your computer in the cloud isn’t for everyone, and I completely understand why many folks wouldn’t or shouldn’t do that for sensitive files. I once built local RAID drives and even airgapped storage systems to avoid having everything online. These things are still possible but getting more expensive by the day as storage prices spike. You’re the best judge of how and where your data should be protected.
That sinking feeling of potentially losing my whole PC? It was immediately followed each time by the assurance that I’d only lost a computer’s body and not its soul. When I got my PC back up and running with new storage, it ended up taking less time to resync all my files than it did to troubleshoot and install new hardware. I can almost hear Billy Crudup doing a Mastercard commercial in my head: New solid state drive, three hundred eighty-nine dollars. Yearly Dropbox subscription, two hundred and three dollars. Never worrying about losing your data? Priceless.

articles.title: La caméra d'action GoPro Max 2 avec enregistrement 8K passe sous la barre des 300 euros
articles.text:
Les vacances sont souvent le moment où l’on capture le plus de souvenirs, mais entre les paysages magnifiques, les activités sportives et les moments imprévus, il n’est pas toujours facile de cadrer la scène parfaite, notamment avec un smartphone. Compactes, résistantes et faciles à transporter, les caméras d’action sont devenues des compagnons incontournables pour immortaliser ses aventures. Avec la GoPro MAX2 en promotion, la marque mise sur une caméra 360 capable de capturer tout ce qui vous entoure.
Sortie en septembre 2025, l’action-cam GoPro MAX2 est normalement vendue 519,99 €. Elle est en ce moment disponible au prix de 293,27 € sur Amazon, ainsi que sur Boulanger.
C’est quoi, cette GoPro MAX2 ?
La GoPro MAX2 reprend le format compact et robuste qui a fait le succès des caméras d’action de la marque. Conçue pour accompagner les activités en extérieur, elle profite d’une conception résistante aux chocs et étanche jusqu’à 5 mètres sans caisson. Son format permet de l’emporter facilement en voyage pour filmer ses souvenirs de vacances, ou pour une randonnée ou une sortie à vélo.
La grande particularité de la GoPro MAX2 repose sur ses deux objectifs capables de filmer à 360 degrés, permettant de capturer toute une scène puis de choisir son cadrage après l’enregistrement grâce au recadrage en post-production. Elle peut enregistrer des vidéos immersives en 8K à 30 images par seconde avec une stabilisation avancée pour conserver des images fluides même en mouvement. Elle propose également un mode grand angle classique pour retrouver une utilisation proche d’une GoPro traditionnelle, selon les besoins.
À ce prix, la GoPro MAX2 est-elle une bonne affaire ?
Moins de 300 €, c’est le budget classique pour une bonne caméra, peu importe la marque. Pour la GoPro MAX2, c’est une très bonne affaire. L’intérêt principal de la GoPro MAX2 repose sur ses nombreuses possibilités créatives. Grâce à la capture 360°, il devient possible de créer des effets de suivi automatique, de modifier son angle après la prise de vue ou encore de réaliser des plans impossibles avec une caméra classique. L’application GoPro Quik permet ensuite de monter rapidement ses vidéos depuis un smartphone, avec des outils de recadrage et d’édition simplifiés.
La caméra profite également des fonctions classiques de GoPro, comme les commandes vocales, les modes accélérés ou encore la compatibilité avec de nombreux accessoires de fixation pour varier les prises de vue. Son autonomie dépend évidemment du mode utilisé, la capture 360° en haute résolution étant plus exigeante, mais comptez au minimum 1h d’utilisation. C’est peu, alors munissez-vous tout de même d’une seconde batterie si vous le pouvez.

articles.title: Dreame, Dyson, Roborock : êtes-vous vraiment obligé d’acheter leurs détergents officiels ?
articles.text:
Dreame, Dyson, Roborock : êtes-vous vraiment obligé d’acheter leurs détergents officiels ?
Quand on achète un nettoyeur de sol, ou un aspirateur-robot-nettoyeur-de-sol, le carton contient souvent un flacon de détergent, destiné spécifiquement à l'appareil. Mais peut-on se diriger vers des produits vendus dans le commerce, plus répandus et moins cher ?
C'est presque un passage obligé : quand on acquiert un appareil destiné à l'entretien des sols comme le Dreame T16 Pro Heat ou le Dyson Spot+Scrub AI, le carton contient, en plus du produit, un flacon d'une solution lavante particulièrement adaptée, nous promet-on, à l'engin. Pire, les fabricants nous interdisent presque l'utilisation de détergents du commerce pourtant bien plus simples à trouver et aussi (et surtout) bien moins chers que ce qui sort de leurs bureaux de R&D.
Toujours un brin méfiants, nous nous sommes donc demandé si tout cela n'était pas un simple moyen pour les constructeurs de maintenir le consommateur dans leur giron et de lui soutirer quelques euros supplémentaires, le long de la durée de vie de l'équipement qu'ils lui auront vendu.
Parole à l'accusé.
Nous avons donc demandé aux fabricants d'appareils pour l'entretien des sols pour quelles raisons ils recommandaient d'utiliser leurs solutions. Si Roborock nous a laconiquement répondu : "Roborock préconise d’utiliser uniquement sa propre solution de nettoyage avec ses appareils et déconseille l’utilisation de détergents ou produits nettoyants tiers", d'autres ont été un peu plus diserts.
Chez Dreame, on invoque des formules corrosives ou trop épaisses qui abîmeraient les composants des équipements : "Les solutions de nettoyage de fabricants tiers peuvent provoquer des problèmes d'adhérence ou obstruer les conduites du robot aspirateur ou de sa station de base. De plus, il n'est pas garanti que certains composants chimiques contenus dans ces solutions n'endommagent pas ou ne corrodent pas le robot aspirateur. En revanche, les solutions de nettoyage officielles Dreame ont fait l'objet de tests complets". Bref, Dreame recommande du Dreame pour les robots et pour les nettoyeurs de sols.
Si le constat est similaire pour les robots ("Nous déconseillons l'usage de détergents, car cela risque d'endommager l'appareil"), les nettoyeurs de sol Rowenta, en revanche, semblent un peu plus résistants que la concurrence chinoise aux formules vendues dans le commerce. Certes "Vous pouvez utiliser le détergent Rowenta dédié", mais "Si vous optez pour un produit du commerce, veillez à ce qu'il ne soit ni trop mousseux ni trop gras (comme le savon noir) pour ne pas encrasser la tuyauterie, et évitez les solutions corrosives (javel, vinaigre blanc)". Cerise sur le gâteau, Rowenta propose même une alternative : "Par sécurité, nous recommandons officiellement le nettoyant multi-surfaces Eucalyptus de Sanytol".
Dyson Clean+Wash Hygiene
Chez Dyson, il existe bien sûr un détergent maison préconisé : "Le produit Dyson 02 a été spécialement formulé pour agir en synergie avec les nettoyeurs de sols durs Dyson tels que le WashG1™, le Dyson Clean+Wash Hygiene™ et le Submarine™. D’autres formules peuvent produire une mousse excessive sur le sol ou être incompatibles avec les plastiques et autres matériaux des appareils". Une formule lavante mainstream serait donc trop mousseuse et il deviendrait très compliqué de rincer les sols. Néanmoins, le Britannique n'exclut pas l'usage de produits du commerce et donne même des conseils : "Pour ceux qui souhaitent utiliser d'autres solutions de nettoyage, veillez à utiliser des produits doux et peu moussants, dilués conformément aux instructions du fabricant" et de souligner "*nous déconseillons l'utilisation d'eau de Javel ou de détergents non dilués dans le réservoir d'eau propre. Il faudrait respecter le dosage recommandé par le fabricant".
La FHER à la rescousse
Comme il n'est jamais très bon de n'entendre qu'un seul son de cloche, nous avons toqué à la porte des professionnels des produits d'hygiène et d'entretien regroupés au sein de la FHER (Fédération Hygiène et Entretien Responsable), ex-AFISE. Selon Virginie D'Enfert, déléguée générale : "les produits d'entretien sont conçus, formulés et testés pour répondre à des usages spécifiques". Traduction, ne mettez pas, disons, une crème à récurer ou du liquide vaisselle dans votre nettoyeur de sol acquis à prix d'or.
Cependant, il serait envisageable d'utiliser un liquide nettoyant pour sols, donc spécifiquement conçu pour cet usage, à quelques conditions toutefois : "Lorsqu'ils sont utilisés avec un équipement électroménager, il est important de s'assurer que le produit choisi est adapté à l'usage recherché et de respecter les consignes d'utilisation associées. Avant toute utilisation, il convient notamment de vérifier les indications figurant sur l'étiquette du produit".
Et il est inutile, voire contre-productif, d'utiliser trop de détergent. rappelle Virginie D'Enfert : "l'efficacité d'un produit repose notamment sur le respect des recommandations d'utilisation indiquées par le fabricant, et en particulier sur le dosage préconisé. Utiliser davantage de produit ne rend pas le nettoyage plus efficace : un surdosage peut au contraire entraîner des désagréments, comme un excès de mousse, des résidus ou un gaspillage inutile".
Alors, que fait-on ?
Si on souhaite absolument utiliser des produits du commerce, on se dirigera vers les produits de nettoyage du sol exclusivement et on évitera ce qui n'est pas prévu strictement pour cet usage : savon noir, liquide vaisselle, produit anticalcaire, lessive… Attention également à la viscosité des produits. Il est préférable que ceux-ci soient bien liquides et pas épais.
Deuxième règle d'or : respecter les dosages. Mais attention, les indications données par les fabricants de détergents concernent un usage manuel. Il sera probablement nécessaire de trouver soi-même la juste dose en débutant par une très petite quantité de produit, quelques gouttes seulement, en augmentant progressivement la concentration si les résultats ne sont pas suffisants. Évidemment, il faudra la diminuer si le sol est recouvert de mousse impossible à éliminer.
Et enfin, il est sage d'être attentif aux réactions de son nettoyeur de sol et à son environnement. Il n'ira sans doute pas jusqu'à faire des bruits suspects ou à vibrer de façon inquiétante. Mais un sol qui ne serait pas assez (ou trop) humide, un excès de mousse qui jaillirait de sous la brosse, une alerte sur l'afficheur du panneau de commande, entre autres comportements inhabituels, sont des signes à ne pas ignorer et il sera préférable d'arrêter l'expérience.
